summary: The former confused remove-curse refusal is resolved: the saved v10 evaluation at be69548a matches all 82 screens and cursors and all 2926 RNG calls. read.c:seffect_remove_curse now traverses eligible inventory and mkobj.c:blessorcurse runs on gameplay objects. The wider source goal remains parked because sit.c:special_throne_effect case 10 and trap.c:domagictrap case 20 lack matching runtime caller evidence; their blocked recipes name the earlier setup and fate conditions.

source.branch: For a noncursed SCR_REMOVE_CURSE read under Confusion, seffect_remove_curse prints the confused You_feel message, traverses inventory while saving obj->nobj before any change, ignores coins and a singleton source scroll, computes wornmask with auxiliary-slot exceptions, and calls blessorcurse(obj,2) for each eligible object before clearing bknown. The same function covers blessed scope, ordinary uncursing, water shop price, steed saddle, punishment, buried ball, and update_inventory.
callers: read.c:seffects dispatches SCR_REMOVE_CURSE and SPE_REMOVE_CURSE to seffect_remove_curse at 2225-2227; js/read.js:seffects currently calls its partial function only for a cursed scroll and otherwise notes the unported gap.
dependencies: mkobj.c:blessorcurse must accept runtime inventory objects without a startup-only assertion and preserve rn2(chance), conditional rn2(2), and curse/bless source effects; js/obj.js currently limits this helper and bless to startup objects.

Inventory traversal must preserve the source next pointer when cursing a secondary weapon moves it out of the chain; related runtime BUC, billing, saddle, unpunish, and buried-ball operations need source-order wiring.

evidence: Saved v10 evaluation challenges/evaluations/20260928083103-v10.json matches 80/82 screens, then diverges at step 80; C next records rn2(2)=1 in blessorcurse(mkobj.c:1846) while JavaScript next calls rn2(5). Recording SHA-256 is 9cb45869824984538232543de4eaefe08fc54fa66f0c7367d0a24d1b7208eb03.

Upstream nethack-c/upstream/src/read.c:1489-1605 defines the whole effect, including the confused inventory loop at 1513-1563 and call to blessorcurse(obj,2) at 1557; mkobj.c:1841-1854 defines the two-stage BUC RNG.

js/read.js:1518-1526 labels only the cursed-scroll arm ported, and js/read.js:2774-2780 skips the noncursed effect. js/obj.js:1692-1704 asserts startup-only BUC objects, and js/obj.js:1563-1568 applies the same restriction to bless.

Current result: challenges/evaluations/20260928203412-v10.json at be69548a77c6899056b335ffae17d07aa1994ea7 matches the case completely: 82/82 screens and cursors, 2926/2926 RNG. Independent ordinary, confused, and learned spell recordings under recordings/read.c/ match exactly.

GOALS.json records source evidence for read.c:seffect_remove_curse while the goal stays parked: the Vlad Tower throne setup is blocked at teleport.c:level_tele/dungeon.c:lev_by_name, and bounded magic-trap C probes did not draw trap.c:domagictrap fate 20.
